title: Zanchi: generic faith ≠ bare fiducia — yet justifying faith nearly is fiducia
source_text: XLV. Zanchius autem fidem in genere acceptam, prout ab ipso supra definita est, a fiducia distinguit, & refellit eos qui dicunt fidem nihil aliud esse quam fiduciam. Quoniam fiducia promissionibus tantum & Evangelio nititur; fides autem ipsam quoque legem respicit, & quicquid est Dei verbum. Tom. 4. lib. 1. cap. 12. tit. De Fide. Sed in eodem capite, titulo De Fiducia, docet fidem qua justificamur aliud non esse revera quam fiduciam, aut certe parum ab ea differre. Unde colligit fidem justificantem & fiduciam idem sunt, vel certe parum inter se differre; & definitionem fidei justificantis, cum fiduciae definitione, eodem redire: Firmus & indubitatus assensus in promissiones Dei de remissione peccatorum, & justitia accipienda, aeternaque vita consequenda a Deo, per & propter filium Jesum Christum, ex afflatu Spiritus Sancti in nobis excitatus. Et quid fiducia? Certissima persuasio de veritate promissionum Dei, qua non dubitamus, quin consecuturi simus, quaecunque nobis simpliciter pro sua gratia pollicitus est Deus: Hoc est enim confidere, idem firmiter credere, & sine ulla haesitatione sperare te habiturum quod ab aliquo tibi promissum est, seu securum esse de rebus promissis propter veritatem promittentis. In Explicatione Theseos primae.
pass_a_gloss: But Zanchi distinguishes faith taken in general, as it was defined by him above, from trust, and refutes those who say faith is nothing other than trust. Because trust rests only on the promises and the Gospel; but faith looks also to the law itself, and whatever is the word of God. Tom. 4, book 1, chapter 12, title On Faith. But in the same chapter, under the title On Trust, he teaches that the faith by which we are justified is in very deed nothing other than trust, or at least differs little from it. Whence he gathers that justifying faith and trust are the same, or at least differ little from each other; and that the definition of justifying faith comes to the same as the definition of trust: A firm and undoubted assent to God's promises concerning remission of sins, and justice to be received, and eternal life to be obtained from God, through and for the sake of the Son Jesus Christ, excited in us by the breathing of the Holy Spirit. And what is trust? A most sure persuasion of the truth of God's promises, by which we do not doubt that we shall obtain whatever God has simply promised us of His grace: For this is to trust — the same as to believe firmly, and without any hesitation to hope that you will have what has been promised you by someone, or to be secure concerning the things promised because of the truth of the promiser. In the Explanation of the first Thesis.
pass_b_english: Zanchi: faith in general ≠ mere fiducia — faith also regards the law and whole Word.
Yet justifying faith is trust, or differs little from it.
Justifying faith = firm undoubted assent to promises of remission, justice, eternal life in Christ — Spirit-excited.
Fiducia = most sure persuasion we shall obtain what God freely promised.
